newsitem.title: YEMEN: Royal yacht Britannia leaves Aden for Oman.
newsitem.headline: Royal yacht Britannia leaves Aden for Oman.

text.p: Britain's royal yacht Britannia left the southern Yemeni port of Aden to Oman on Sunday en route to Hong Kong on its final voyage, officials said.
The governor of Aden and other officials attended a ceremony bidding farewell to the 6,000-tonne mini-liner.
Yemeni President Ali Abdullah Saleh visited the ship on Saturday evening and met British and Yemeni businessmen at the end of a seminar on investments in the impoverished Arab state.

The yacht, being taken out of service after the current tour ending 44 years afloat, docked on Thursday at the Red Sea port of Hodeida at the start of a three-day visit to Yemen, its first port of call in the Middle East.
The ship hosted a symposium entitled "Invest in Yemen", which was touted by the local press as a "milestone in Yemeni-U.K. business".
Until 1967 Britain ruled Aden directly and the rest of Yemen indirectly through a protectorate agreement with local sultans.

The Britannia has been to Yemen, a small oil-producer country with 16 million people, seven times between 1959 and 1993. On its fourth visit in 1986, it helped evacuate hundreds of Britons and other foreign nationals during clashes in former South Yemen.
From Oman, the Britannia will visit the United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Kuwait and Bahrain.
